items.ref: TECH-SPEC.md:199 only lists #960 in a prose paragraph ('v1 issues of this class'); it is absent from every GP test's issue-id column (GP3 lists #1107 #1299 #1212 #897 #910 #1179 #1261 — no #960); ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r2.md:288 proposed a fix but left it in the 'Rows without a verdict' section
items.archaeology: git log --all -S 'mcp_tool' in cm-main surfaces e479068a 'feat(antigravity-cli): bounded PreToolUse enforcement via agy's native decision contract' and 9f34c6f1 'Add GitHub Copilot CLI + Antigravity CLI (agy) support (#787)' as the commits that grew the PreToolUse matcher surface across adapters — each new agent added its own mcp_tool-shaped matcher, which is how the matcher ended up firing on every mcp__ tool instead of only context-mode's. ORIGINAL_INTENT (ADR-0008 item 4 comment): 'Claude Code: the PreToolUse hook is type:"mcp_tool", so it runs only while this session's server is connected; otherwise the tool runs' — this describes availability gating, not a tool-name filter, so the overly-broad matcher firing on unrelated MCP tools (e.g. mcp__grafana__get_datasource) was never addressed by that ADR. REGRESSION_RISK: HIGH if v2 keeps the same type:"mcp_tool" matcher shape without a name filter — it reintroduces #960 exactly, spawning a hook process (and its node cold-start cost, also #951/#953 territory) on every unrelated MCP tool call. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: matcher must filter by tool name (e.g. regex/string on mcp__context-mode__ or the adapter table's own prefix), not just hook event type; per P2 hooks are hint-only and must not be the thing deciding cost.
regressions: If PreToolUse matcher stays type:"mcp_tool" only, v2 reintroduces #960 for any non-context-mode MCP server the host also runs.
items.question: Does the v2 adapter table's generated PreToolUse matcher filter by tool name (mcp__context-mode__*) in addition to event type "mcp_tool", so that calls like mcp__grafana__get_datasource spawn no hook process?
items.recommendation: r2's verdict of 'needs-decision, Rows without a verdict' is still correct and unresolved — DECISIONS-r3.md does not settle it. This is a genuine gap: TECH-SPEC references #960 only in prose, no GP test asserts the matcher excludes non-ctx MCP tools. Add a GP3 case: given a call to an unrelated mcp__ tool, assert zero hook process spawned, before closing this.

items.ref: TECH-SPEC.md GP4 issue column explicitly lists #951 ('NODE_OPTIONS does not leak' is a named GP4 assertion)
items.archaeology: git log --all -S 'NODE_OPTIONS' in cm-main shows the preload mechanism has existed since early batch_execute concurrency work (1d991a22/7cd92c4a 'feat(batch_execute): opt-in concurrency for I/O-bound batches', c2d390a5 'feat: FS tracking for batch_execute'). ORIGINAL_INTENT: NODE_OPTIONS preload was added to inject FS tracking/instrumentation into spawned processes; it was never cleaned up per-process, so stale cm-fs-preload-<pid>.js paths leaked into sibling processes after the owning server exited. REGRESSION_RISK: if v2 keeps any NODE_OPTIONS-based preload for sandboxed execution (needed for FS tracking/stats), the same leak reappears unless the preload path is removed from env before process exit or scoped per spawn rather than per machine-global env var. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: env must be passed via spawn env only (map-I3 #925's own requirement text), never process.env mutation that outlives the spawn.
regressions: Any v2 FS-tracking/instrumentation mechanism that reuses NODE_OPTIONS process-wide (vs. per-spawn env) reintroduces #951.
items.question: none, GP4 names the exact assertion
items.recommendation: Verify GP4's 'NODE_OPTIONS does not leak' test actually starts two sequential server processes (server A exits, server B runs) as the ticket's Given/When/Then describes, not just a single-process check.

items.ref: TECH-SPEC GP4 issue list includes #925 directly; GP4 asserts 'env passed via spawn env, never string-prefixed into the command'
items.archaeology: git log --all --grep '#925' found nothing directly, but 358673d9 'fix: handle batch env prefix by shell (#407)' is the related v1 fix for the general class of 'env handling breaks certain shell constructs' bugs — same mechanism family (string-prefixing env vars into the command line instead of passing them via spawn options). ORIGINAL_INTENT (commit 358673d9): v1 built commands like 'VAR=val cmd' textually per-shell, which breaks any command starting with a shell keyword (if/for/() because the env-var prefix gets glued in front of the keyword instead of being passed as spawn-level env. REGRESSION_RISK: if v2's executor still constructs a textual env-prefixed command string for any shell (even one), #925 reappears for that shell specifically — the ticket's acceptance test ('if true; then echo ok; fi') is a direct regression probe for 358673d9's fix shape.
regressions: Any shell path that still builds 'VAR=val <command>' as a string (rather than passing env via the spawn() options object) regresses #925.

items.recommendation: Confirm GP4's env-spawn test is run against every shell in TECH-SPEC's language list (shell, powershell, +runtimes on PATH), not just POSIX sh, since 358673d9's bug was shell-specific.
